quote: Language models (LMs) are versatile interfaces to knowledge, capable of remarkably complex linguistic tasks. Summarization of complex documents, reasoning over long passages of text and zero-shot inference in specialist domains such as medicine are a few examples that demonstrate their abilities.
datasets: distribution dataset with associated question-answer pairs
American Community Survey (ACS) Public Use Microdata Sample (PUMS)
outputs: numerical responses (e.g., percentiles, samples, probabilities) in probabilistic reasoning tasks

quote: We sample LM responses 10 times per question with a random seed. Then, we elect to average and effectively use all answers as a part of our final evaluation in order to help capture the variability in language model responses and provide a broader understanding of their reasoning capabilities. This effectively is a form of self-consistency.
All results are reported as Mean Absolute Error (MAE) ± Standard Error (σ_M) with (%) units.
